evals.prompt: Quick clean-code pass on this diff before I commit?
evals.expected_output: Uses the quick gear: one read-through against docs/clean-code-standard.md, findings reported inline with file:line and severity, no subagents and no report file, respecting the 'where this bends' notes.
assertions: Uses the quick gear for a small diff (inline findings, no report file, no subagents)
Reports each finding with file:line, the principle, the reader-cost, a concrete suggestion, and a severity
Honours the 'where this bends' notes (no false-DRY, speculative-abstraction, or over-extraction findings)
Says so plainly if nothing meaningful is wrong instead of manufacturing findings

evals.prompt: Do a thorough clean-code review of the whole payments module.
evals.expected_output: Uses the deep gear: two-stage analyzer->reviewer verification, writing docs/reports/clean-code/CLEAN-CODE-REPORT-<date>.md via the report template; apply stays opt-in.
assertions: Uses the deep gear for a module-sized scope
Dispatches a read-only analyzer then an independent reviewer that re-verifies every finding
Creates git-excluded docs/reports/clean-code/ and writes the report using references/report-template.md
Does not apply changes unless explicitly asked (review stops at findings)

evals.prompt: This 400-line OrderService class is a mess — is it clean?
evals.expected_output: Flags line-level craft, but recognises the god-class/SRP problem as structural and defers it up-ladder to /solid rather than solving architecture under the clean-code lens.
assertions: Reports line-level craft findings (names, long functions, comments) against the standard
Identifies the single-responsibility / god-class problem as structural
Defers the structural fix up-ladder to /solid (and names /gof, /ddd, or /clean-architecture where relevant) instead of redesigning under clean-code
Keeps the hand-offs as a distinct section, not clean-code fixes

evals.prompt: We're doing a SOLID refactor — will the extracted classes end up clean?
evals.expected_output: Explains the substrate role: because the shared implementer role and tdd link docs/clean-code-standard.md, code produced by any lens's refactor is clean by construction — no separate clean-code invocation is needed for that.
assertions: Explains that clean-code is a substrate linked by the shared implementer role and tdd
States that /solid, /gof, and /clean-architecture refactors come out clean by construction
Points at docs/clean-code-standard.md as the single source of truth consumers link (never copy)
Distinguishes the ambient substrate role from the invoked standalone review
